raw_response:
I have farmed these fields long enough to know that I should not bet everything on one crop, especially at my age. Chili brings better cash if the market is decent, but it needs much more labor and more careful water and pest management. Wheat and maize are steadier for me, and on part of the land I will keep the wheat-maize rotation because it spreads risk and fits what I know well. I only have 10.1 mu and three people in the household, so labor is a real constraint. Because of that, I will not push chili onto all the land. I will keep about 6.1 mu in chili and 4.0 mu in wheat followed by summer maize on the same 4.0 mu. I have well water, so I can protect yield when the season turns dry, but pumping costs money, so I will irrigate by crop stage rather than too often.

For wheat, I will stay with a moderate input plan, not the highest one. I usually aim for stable yield, around 430 to 470 kg per mu, with nitrogen split between basal and jointing. For maize after wheat, the turnaround is tight, so I will use rotary tillage and sow quickly after harvest, with one basal application and one topdress if the stand looks strong enough. Chili is where I will spend more attention. I will use improved seedlings, base fertilizer before transplanting, then small topdressings after establishment and around fruit set. I will watch aphids, thrips, and disease closely because once chili gets hit badly, the loss is painful. I am managing for steady income and manageable work, not for the absolute maximum yield.
